messages:
julian: Planning Terraform apply for tonight's release window (2026-03-21 22:00 UTC). Scope: rotate IAM role trust policy for cross-account access, update KMS key alias to new naming convention, and pin provider to avoid drift. Requesting deploybot slot + serial apply. Plan excerpt:
```
# module.iam_role will be updated
~ resource aws_iam_role.trusted_role
~ resource aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.trust_attach
# module.kms will update alias target
~ resource aws_kms_alias.app_alias
```
Please review rollback steps and smoke tests. @sre-oncall can you take a look? :eyes:

anna: :eyes: Can we split the KMS alias change from the role rotation? KMS change is low blast radius but the role trust touches cross-account consumers.

mike: +1 to splitting. Order suggestion: 1) IAM role rotation, validate, 2) KMS alias update. Keep tfstate lock between steps and don't push both in one apply.

julian: OK doing two serial applies. Step 1: `terraform apply -target=module.iam_role -auto-approve` then wait 10m, run smoke tests. Step 2: `terraform apply -target=module.kms -auto-approve`. Will pin provider in both modules.

deploy-bot: deploybot queued job 2034567890. Slot reserved for 2026-03-21 22:00 UTC. Workspace: prod. Lock acquired. Metadata: {"release":"2026-03-21","ticket":"ENGOPS-412"}.

sre-oncall: Quick checklist: 1) Preapply plan uploaded, 2) tfstate snapshot taken, 3) smoke tests ready. Rollback plan: if role rotation breaks cross-account assume, restore previous tfstate snapshot (s3://redwood-tfstate/backups/2026-03-20T21:50Z) and reapply that snapshot in emergency. Also have a short DNS-level fallback for kms alias (if needed).

anna: Add automated health checks: lambda invocation smoke test and consumer auth check. Abort criteria: >5% auth failures over 2m after step1 => abort and restore tfstate. Document thresholds in runbook.

julian: Adding smoke tests now. Also pin provider in root modules:
```hcl
required_providers {
  aws = { version = "~> 4.3.2" }
}
```
This avoids accidental upgrade to v5 behaviors during apply.

mike: We'll run `terraform plan -out=preapply.plan` and attach artifact to the release ticket before starting. Also suggest running the plan with `-refresh=false` to keep timing consistent.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook updated: /runbooks/iam-rotation-2026-03-21.md. Contingency steps added: restore tfstate backup from 2026-03-20T21:50Z, circuit-breaker: stop writes to cross-account queue for 15m, escalate to oncall if rollback fails.

julian: Decision summary: perform staggered apply (IAM first, KMS second) in the 22:00 UTC slot. Serial across regions/AZs: 3 partitions with 2m wait between partitions. Owner: julian. If smoke tests fail, trigger rollback plan above. Please react with :thumbsup: to approve.

anna: :thumbsup:

mike: :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploybot started apply job 2034567890-step1 for module.iam_role. Logging to /var/log/deploybot/2034567890-step1.log. Short tail:
```
2026-03-21T22:00:05Z apply: refreshing state...
2026-03-21T22:00:22Z apply: updating aws_iam_role.trusted_role...
2026-03-21T22:01:10Z apply: completed with 0 errors
```
Keep monitoring `infra.iam.rotation` dashboard in Datadog.
